questions.help:
7 Seat belts
 
7.1 Purpose and effectiveness
The purpose of a seat belt is to retain and protect the driver and occupants in the event of sudden stopping, collision or the vehicle rolling over. The seat belt prevents the occupants of a vehicle from being catapulted out of it and absorbs part of the energy of an impact.
During a frontal collision against an indeformable object, a vehicle stops in a tenth of a second, but due to inertia, the occupants will continue moving at the same speed as the vehicle was travelling at. Therefore, there is the likelihood of colliding with the steering wheel or the windshield, which will result in serious injuries being sustained.
To avoid this, the seat belt slows the movement of the body by stretching out, as if is made of an elastic material, by an extensible action.
(Página 75 del manual 'Learning to drive')

7 Seat belts    
     
7.6 Misconceptions of safety belts
“It is dangerous to use a seat belt during pregnancy”
The use of seat belts is compulsory for pregnant women, as they have proved that if you are not wearing it, the foetus can suffer major damage in the event of an accident.
The abdominal belt must go as low as possible on the hips, to wear it higher could potentially harm the baby. There are devices on the market that adequately prevent the belt from going up onto the abdomen.
“The belt is only necessary for front seat passengers. In the rear seats it isn’ necessary”
If passengers in the rear seats fail to wear a seat belt there is the probability that, in the event of a frontal collision, they will be fired forwards towards the occupants in the front seats and serious injury will be caused.
The likelihood for an occupant in the rear seats to cause the death of another passenger in the front seats due to the fact that they are launched forward is up to 8 times greater than if the seat belt is worn.
(Página 78 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
Road traffic collisions  
   
1 A public health problem
Moreover, in addition to the human drama, it is important to highlight the enormous economic impact (either directly or indirectly) that occurs as a result of a traffic collision.
Costs derived from road traffic accidents are classified as human, material, healthcare and administrative.
Human costs include the loss of lives, productive capacity and physical and psychological suffering. Material costs consist of damages caused on vehicles and their loads as well as on the road and the environment. Healthcare costs comprise first aid, care and treatment of the wounded, rehabilitation and adaptations. Administrative costs hold those of police officers and firefighters and insurance and services management.
People believe that an accident has little effect on them but the cost is borne by taxpayers. The cost of vehicle insurance is also affected, as premiums are affected by collision data and the cost of accidents.
For these reasons, various international organisations, including the World Health Organisation (WHO), believe that road collisions are a priority public health problem throughout the world.
There is a serious need to work together to reduce the high numbers of dead and seriously injured on the roads.
(Página 248 del manual 'Learning to drive')

If, after the indicated period, it has not been presented to the aforementioned inspection, the Traffic Department will initiate the procedure for withdrawing the vehicle from circulation.
The age of the vehicle is calculated with effect from the date that it was first registered or from the date when it was granted the right to be used.
(Página 25 del manual 'Learning to drive')

ACTIVE SAFETY FEATURES  
 
3 Brakes
3.4 Braking performance
The braking performance depends upon:
The correct state of maintenance and care of the braking system.
The correct pressure (application) being applied on the brake pedal that ultimately leads to the necessary pressure being transmitted to the brakes. The greater the force applied to the pedal, the greater the pressure that is exerted on the drum shoes or the disc pads of the brakes and therefore the result is more effective braking.
The condition of the tyres and adhesion quality of the tyres onto the road surface.
The condition of the road surface, the speed and the mass of the vehicle and its load.
The proper distribution of brake action on all wheels.
(Página 65 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
10 Head restraints
 
Head restraints are very effective in the event of a collision, avoiding or reducing the severity of injuries to the neck or vertebrates caused by the sudden movement, forward and back, of the head (whiplash). It is therefore imperative to properly use them, both in front and back seats.
Whiplash occurs when a person’s head moves backward and then forward suddenly with great force. It is particularly frequent in rear- ending collisions.
As well as muscle and head pain it can cause decreased neck mobility, vertigo or dizziness, among other symptoms.
(Página 80 del manual 'Learning to drive')
